gates.reason: Checked state-root/worktree containment, symlink rejection, fixed subprocess argument arrays, Sidekick-ledger root confinement, and tool-free bounded judge dispatch; no exploitable traversal, injection, secret egress, or unsafe write defect survived inspection.

Checked receipt digests, trial/arm identity binding, evidence re-derivation, canonical Run reconstruction, metric derivation, artifact coverage, and durable content-addressed publication; no reproducible integrity defect found.
The sealer retains every evidence object in memory until publication while enforcing only per-object limits, permitting aggregate memory use far beyond the diff budget.

findings.title: Seal assembly has no aggregate memory budget for retained evidence
findings.what: Each evidence file may be as large as 256 MiB, and the expected set can contain many files across every arm and judging attempt. sealTrial reads all of them into Buffers and addObject retains those Buffers in objectMap.objects until the later staging write. Unlike worktree diffs, ordinary evidence has no aggregate byte limit, so a structurally valid large trial can exhaust process memory before publication.
findings.fix: Track aggregate retained object bytes and reject the trial against a documented total bundle-memory budget, or stream each content-addressed object into staging while retaining only its digest and manifest metadata.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing multiple individually valid evidence files whose combined size exceeds the configured aggregate budget is rejected before all bytes are retained; a within-budget fixture still seals, and a memory probe demonstrates peak RSS remains within the documented budget.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the size constants, complete expected-evidence enumeration, accumulation loop, and delayed write loop. The only aggregate byte cap applies to worktree diffs; no aggregate cap or streaming path covers the evidence Buffers retained in objectMap.objects.
